brief.headline: Cut ₹28.69 L/yr in overpay and shift 15 days faster payment for another ₹8.01 L cash — we're 47.43% of their business.

priceAsk.summary: Bring their prices down to match Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic on the top three items, then apply that drop across the board.
priceAsk.target: Save ₹28.69 L/yr by closing the gap to our cheapest supplier
priceAsk.basis: We pay Mars Plastics ₹0.81/NOS for the 28 mm PP cap; Cincorp charges us ₹1.08/NOS — a 33.2% gap worth ₹14.05 L/yr on that one item alone. The market asking price sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, so our Mars price of ₹0.81 is already strong, and Cincorp has room to come down. Same story on the HDPE bottle (10.7% gap, ₹7.88 L) and the measuring cup (30.6% gap, ₹6.75 L).

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days payment, freeing up ₹16.02 L cash for us; they already take 39d to pay their own suppliers — longer than similar firms at 23d — so tighter terms for us are only fair.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹16.02 L cash freed up for us at 30 days; another ₹8.01 L if we go to 15 days faster

brief.financialLeverage: They're small — ₹4.11 Cr in sales — and we buy ₹1.95 Cr, so 47.43% of everything they sell comes from us. That's huge leverage. They keep only 6.0% of every ₹100 they sell, much less than similar firms (15.0%), so price cuts hurt them more than most. But they owe 1.13× their own cash and their cash is stuck for 101 days (similar firms: 107d), so they need our cash flow. Push hard on payment terms and the price gaps to our other suppliers; they can't afford to lose us.

evidence.figure: ₹1.95 Cr our spend vs ₹4.11 Cr their revenue = 47.43%

evidence.point: Paying ₹28.69 L/yr more than our cheapest supplier for the same sort of items
evidence.figure: ₹28.69 L total gap vs best price we pay

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100) — they make pharma bottles and caps, a perfect second source to pressure Cincorp and cover our risk.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed, ₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B (73/100) — strong in rigid pharma packaging (bottles, closures), a credible alternate if Cincorp can't meet our price.

risks: They're a small entity (under ₹10 Cr) flagged for verification — confirm their production capacity can handle our ₹1.95 Cr/yr steadily before locking in long commitments.

They keep much less profit than rivals (6.0% vs 15.0%) and owe 1.13× their own cash — pushing too hard on price could squeeze them into supply hiccups; balance the price ask with faster payment (which costs us nothing but gives them cash relief).
Their Altman Z-score is 1.83 (grey zone) — not distress, but not robust either; line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek now so we have a second source ready if their finances tighten.

We're 47.43% of their sales — if they lose us, they're in real trouble, so they'll fight to keep the business; use that, but don't burn the bridge — we need reliable supply, not a desperate supplier cutting corners.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹28.69 lakh more than our other suppliers for similar items — let's close that gap and talk about how faster payment from us can help your cash flow.
